# Proving Ground bench

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Zero-dependency program tasks in several domains, registered from `environments/<task>/task.json` files and run through the harness's own agent loop or through the product's own loop, compared in frozen paired experiments. [`SUMMARY.md`](SUMMARY.md) documents the tiers whose verdict rests on cases the implementer never sees; [`plans/README.md`](plans/README.md) documents the checked-in experiment and fleet plans; [`packages/improvement/environments/README.md`](../../../../../packages/improvement/environments/README.md) documents the registry service every task registers against.

## The completion family

[`tools/synthesize-completion-tasks.mjs`](tools/synthesize-completion-tasks.mjs) multiplies the 44 hand-authored environments into completion tasks: for each parent environment and each top-level function of its reference program, it writes a child under `environments-completion/<parent>--<function>/` whose workspace holds the reference solution with that one function's body replaced by `throw new Error('not implemented')` (the signature and any leading comment or JSDoc kept), whose `test/` and `package.json` are the parent's, unchanged, and whose prompt is the parent's prompt plus a paragraph naming the file and function to complete and forbidding edits elsewhere. [`register-completion-environments.ts`](register-completion-environments.ts) registers whatever the factory admitted, under the same `bench` kind the curated 44 use, with `detail.family` naming the parent and `detail.completion` naming the stubbed file and function; the [`with-completion`](overlays/with-completion.cordis.yml) overlay mounts it as a second producer beside the curated one, and [`with-completion-openrouter`](overlays/with-completion-openrouter.cordis.yml) mounts it beside the free open-weight route `with-openrouter` names.

A completion child's `checks` are its parent's, hidden cases included, so a child is judged the way its parent's tier is judged: a child of a tier-2 to tier-4 parent certifies when the visible suite under `test/` passes, and a child of a tier-5 or tier-6 parent also answers to the cases its parent's validator holds back (`reference/cases.json`, copied through), with the same hidden-case rule appended to its prompt that the curated registrar appends. `admit.mjs` and the factory's own `--admit` step admit only a child whose pre-state fails its own visible test suite and whose reference passes it and, where a check carries cases, only a child whose stub fails at least one case and whose reference passes every case; `environments-completion/REFUSED.json` records every candidate function the factory generated but admission refused, and why — a function the parent's visible suite never reaches, or one no held-back case exercises, so stubbing it changes nothing that check can see fail. The checked-in run over the 44 admitted all 246 and refused none, so the file is `[]`.

Every completion child inherits its parent's `heldOut` flag, so a family never straddles the held-out split: either every function stubbed from one reference program is training-eligible, or all of them are held out, matching whichever side the parent itself was assigned to.

## The repository-derived family

[`tools/synthesize-repository-tasks.ts`](tools/synthesize-repository-tasks.ts) derives function-implementation tasks from this repository's own tested code: for every module under `packages/util/<package>/src/*.ts` whose spec under `tests/` imports only that module and `vitest`, binds only `describe`, `it`, `test`, and `expect`, and asserts only through the matcher subset [`tools/expect-shim.mjs`](tools/expect-shim.mjs) implements (listed under the public-repository family below, each with `.not`), and for every exported function of that module that carries a JSDoc block, it writes a child under `environments-repository/<package>--<function>/`: the module transpiled to plain ESM JavaScript by the TypeScript compiler with that one function's body replaced by `throw new Error('not implemented')` (every other export intact), a `README.md` that is task content (the prompt plus the type declarations the build erased), the transpiled reference under `reference/src/`, and under `reference/cases.json` one hidden case per `it` block that exercises the function — a self-contained ESM program `node --input-type=module` reads from standard input, exit 0 on pass and non-zero with the assertion message on fail, so a case runs under plain `node` with no test runner installed. The prompt names the file, the function, and hands over the JSDoc and the TypeScript signature; it never reveals the spec. A spec outside those rules is skipped with the reason printed, and the census the factory prints counts candidates, skips by reason, and admitted children. [`register-repository-environments.ts`](register-repository-environments.ts) registers whatever the factory admitted under the same `bench` kind, in domain `repository`, with `detail.repository` naming the package, module, and spec and `detail.completion` naming the stubbed file and function; the [`with-repository`](overlays/with-repository.cordis.yml) overlay mounts it as a second producer beside the curated one.

A repository child is judged on its hidden cases alone: its workspace holds no test, `admit.mjs` admits only a child whose stub fails at least one case and whose reference passes every case, and the factory's `--admit` step deletes what admission refuses and records why in `environments-repository/REFUSED.json`. A child's tier follows the number of cases that exercise its function (`--tier-bands`, default `4,12`: tier 2 below four cases, tier 3 below twelve, tier 4 from twelve on), and every child is `heldOut: false`, since the family has no parent whose split it could inherit. The checked-in run over `packages/util` reads 14 modules of 7 packages and derives from one: seven modules have no spec that imports them (the six `invariant.ts` companions and `dsh-brand`), three specs bind `vi` or `afterEach`, two import `node:fs/promises` or `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, and `dsh-native-command` exports no block-bodied function; `@deepseek-ai/dsh-output-retention` yields two tier-3 children, `describeOmitted` with seven cases and `formatRetentionNotice` with four, both admitted, so `REFUSED.json` is `[]`.

## The public-repository family

[`tools/synthesize-public-tasks.ts`](tools/synthesize-public-tasks.ts) derives the same kind of task from permissively licensed public JavaScript and TypeScript repositories. [`tools/public-sources.json`](tools/public-sources.json) is the allowlist: for each source its name, clone URL, the full commit the factory reads and nothing else, the SPDX id of its licence, the licence file's path and SHA-256, the directory mirrored into a child's `src/`, and the directories read. The factory fetches each commit one deep into the gitignored cache `.proving-ground/public-sources/<name>` and drops, with the reason in the census, a source whose fetch fails, whose licence file is missing or digests differently, whose licence text reads as another id than the one declared, or whose id is outside MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, and Apache-2.0 — the licences whose terms admit a derived task as training material with attribution kept; a copyleft or unlicensed source is never read. It then reads every test file under the listed directories (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, a bare `test.*`) whose imports are a supported runner — `vitest` or `@jest/globals` by named bindings, or no runner at all under their globals, for the `expect` family; `node:test` with `node:assert` for the node family — plus `node:` built-ins and relative imports that resolve under the source root, followed through `export { x } from`, `export { default as x } from`, and `export * from` chains to the files that declare them (a namespace import becomes a frozen object of the members the test reads); a package import rejects the test. The modules a test imports are the modules it judges, and for every exported function of such a module that carries a JSDoc block — a function exported by a later `export default name` or `export { name }` counts, and an implementation preceded by overload signatures inherits the first overload's JSDoc — it writes a child under `environments-public/<source>--<function>/`: the module's dependency closure transpiled to plain ESM JavaScript under `src/` with that one function's body replaced by `throw new Error('not implemented')`, [`tools/expect-shim.mjs`](tools/expect-shim.mjs) as `test/expect-shim.mjs` for an `expect` suite, the source's licence text as `LICENSE`, a `README.md` that is task content (the prompt, an attribution section naming the source, commit, licence, and copyright line, and the type declarations the build erased), `package.json`, the untouched closure under `reference/src/`, and under `reference/cases.json` one hidden case per test block that exercises the function, pooled across every test that imports the module and capped at `--max-cases` (default 60) spread evenly over them. A case is the shim import, the test's imports re-pointed at the workspace, and one block per level as the repository family assembles them. A block is dropped on its own, counted by reason, when its body or an enclosing level's own statements reach `vi` or `mock`, a matcher outside the subset, `.resolves`/`.rejects`/`expect.*`, a hook, a nested runner call, or `require`/`import()`; a block registered through `it.each`, `it.skip`, a loop, an options object, or a non-literal title is skipped and counted by form. The prompt names the file, the function, the source, its commit and licence, the closure's other files, and the shim, hands over the JSDoc and the signature, and never reveals the tests. The shim implements `toBe`, `toEqual`, `toStrictEqual`, `toMatchObject`, `toBeUndefined`, `toBeDefined`, `toBeNull`, `toBeNaN`, `toBeTruthy`, `toBeFalsy`, `toBeTypeOf`, `toBeInstanceOf`, `toHaveLength`, `toHaveProperty`, `toContain`, `toContainEqual`, `toThrow` and its alias `toThrowError`, `toThrowErrorMatchingInlineSnapshot`, `toMatch`, `toBeGreaterThan`, `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual`, `toBeLessThan`, `toBeLessThanOrEqual`, and `toBeCloseTo`, each with `.not`, and the runtime no-ops `expectTypeOf` and `assertType`.

A public child is judged on its hidden cases alone, exactly as a repository child is: the factory runs the pooled cases against the reference twice and drops any it fails in either run — the shim or the transform falling short of a block, or a block whose verdict depends on the host's load, such as a real-timer debounce test, which must not decide a cell — keeps per function the cases its stub fails, tiers the child by that count under the same `--tier-bands`, and its `--admit` step runs `admit.mjs`, deletes what admission refuses, and writes `environments-public/REFUSED.json` and `environments-public/CENSUS.json` — per source the fetch status and reason, modules, tests, usable tests, rejections by category, blocks dropped by reason and skipped by form, candidates, written, and admitted; overall the skips by reason, the cases the reference failed, and the written and admitted counts by tier. Every child is `heldOut: false` and carries in `task.json` the source's URL, commit, licence id, licence digest, and copyright line under `public`, and under `terms` the data-use purposes its licence admits (`delivery`, `training`, `evaluation`) with `attribution: LICENSE`, the file that must travel with the task and anything derived from it; a trajectory on such a child is training material only where the route's own terms admit training too. [`register-public-environments.ts`](register-public-environments.ts) registers whatever the factory admitted under the `bench` kind, in domain `public`, with `detail.public`, `detail.terms`, and `detail.completion`, and the [`with-public`](overlays/with-public.cordis.yml) overlay mounts it as a second producer beside the curated one. The checked-in run reads ten pinned sources — es-toolkit, remeda, simple-statistics, @antfu/utils, case-anything, string-ts, ms, date-fns, ufo, and change-case, nine MIT and one ISC — 2,027 modules and 808 test files, 537 of which yield at least one block; 271 are rejected whole: 202 import a package (195 of them date-fns's), 32 import outside the source root (31 of them remeda's helpers under its `test/` directory), 31 keep no block once their unsupported forms are set aside, and 6 of string-ts's import nothing under test. 627 documented functions reach a stub run and 560 become children — 224 of tier 2, 240 of tier 3, and 96 of tier 4; 189 from es-toolkit, 142 from remeda, 81 from simple-statistics, 48 each from string-ts and date-fns, 21 from @antfu/utils, 16 from case-anything, 8 from ufo, 4 from ms, and 3 from change-case — while 65 are reached by no case and 2 repeat a name already taken in their source; 27 functions without a JSDoc block, 2 with an empty body, 2 whose module closure cannot be built, and 1 whose module's reference passes no case never reach that run, and the reference fails 4 of the pooled cases, which are dropped. Admission keeps all 560, so `REFUSED.json` is `[]`.
